title: The Lane Nobody Claimed

cast.ada: Ada Lin, a municipal relay runner

rule: The calibration cabinet stays locked unless its single brass key turns the lock; it has no electronic release or duplicate key during this story.
deceased: Coach Roland died two years before the meet and never returns alive in present action.

chapters.title: A Space on the Card

facts.subject: char:ada
facts.anchor: Ada remained in the warm-up hall when the first session ended.

facts.subject: item:relay_card
facts.anchor: Ada handed the relay card to Nessa, who tucked it inside her zipped vest.

facts.subject: org:relay_team
facts.anchor: The ten-pound entry payment reduced their travel fund from ninety-four pounds to eighty-four.

facts.subject: char:nessa
facts.anchor: The registrar entered Nessa as the registered reserve runner, not a spectator.

facts.subject: char:ada
facts.object: fresh shallow scrape on left palm
facts.anchor: The rough starting block scraped Ada’s left palm, leaving a shallow red line.

facts.subject: item:timing_clock
facts.anchor: Imani set the timing clock on the bench in the warm-up hall.

facts.subject: char:imani
facts.anchor: Imani was alive and counting the entrants aloud beside the bench.

facts.subject: item:relay_card
facts.anchor: The official stamp made the relay entry provisional until both runners checked in.

claim: The cabinet has a second key.
“The cabinet has a second key,” Nessa said, repeating a rumour she had heard outside.
trueClaim: “There are eighty-four pounds left,” Ada said after counting the notes.

cognitions.content: Nessa is officially registered as the reserve runner.
cognitions.anchor: Ada read Nessa’s reserve registration herself and now knew it was official.

cognitions.content: Ada will ask her to run if a place opens.
cognitions.anchor: Nessa believed Ada would ask her to run if a place opened, although Ada had made no promise.

cognitions.content: The card’s notch once served a timing purpose.
cognitions.anchor: Imani suspected the notch had once served a timing purpose; its shape alone did not prove that.
Until she read the register, Ada had wrongly believed Nessa had come only to watch.

correction.content: Nessa came as a registered reserve, not merely a spectator.
correction.anchor: The register corrected that mistake: Nessa had come as a runner.

relationship: Ada agreed to share the practice lane with Nessa, but kept their conversation formal.
memory: Years before the meet, Ada had waited alone on the outdoor track while Roland packed the hurdles.
hooks: A crescent notch interrupted the relay card’s margin, and neither runner could explain it.
Four empty boxes remained beneath the team’s names, with no heading to explain what belonged there.
A blue cord was knotted around the clock handle, although Imani had never tied it there.
chapters.plan: Tomorrow, Ada intended to ask the registrar to make Nessa a starter.
chapters.hypothesis: If the cabinet had a remote release, they could open it from the track; it had no such release.
chapters.dream: In her nap Ada dreamed that Roland ran the final leg, but she woke to the empty bench.
chapters.uncertainty: The mark beside the notch might have been a worn numeral, but Ada could not identify it.

chapters.title: The Exchange Zone

facts.subject: char:ada
facts.anchor: Ada stayed at the municipal relay track after the afternoon exchange trials.

facts.subject: item:relay_card
facts.anchor: Nessa passed the relay card to Imani for the official handover trial.

facts.subject: org:relay_team
facts.anchor: A six-pound entry rebate increased the travel fund from eighty-four pounds to ninety.

facts.subject: char:nessa
facts.anchor: The registrar changed Nessa’s status from reserve to confirmed relay starter.

facts.subject: char:ada
facts.anchor: By the afternoon, the scrape on Ada’s left palm had formed a dry scab without fresh bleeding.

facts.subject: item:timing_clock
facts.anchor: Imani carried the timing clock to the table inside the municipal relay track.

facts.subject: item:brass_key
facts.anchor: Imani placed the cabinet’s single brass key in Ada’s hand.

facts.subject: item:relay_card
facts.anchor: Both check-in signatures changed their relay entry from provisional to confirmed.

claim: “Roland invented that notch,” Nessa said, then admitted that nobody had told her so.
trueClaim: “We have ninety pounds now,” Imani said, pointing to the new balance.

cognitions.content: She is now a confirmed starter.
cognitions.anchor: The registrar told Nessa directly that she was now a confirmed starter.

cognitions.content: Nessa will hold the exchange position.
cognitions.anchor: Ada believed Nessa would hold the exchange position, based on the last three clean trials.

cognitions.content: The blank boxes concern later meets.
cognitions.anchor: Imani suspected the blank boxes concerned later meets, but the unused forms gave no answer.

cognitions.content: Ada asked the registrar to promote her.
cognitions.anchor: Nessa initially misread the change as proof that Ada had asked for her promotion.

correction.content: The registrar promoted her from her trial time, without Ada making the request.
correction.anchor: The registrar explained that the trial time alone had earned the promotion; Ada had not requested it.

relationship: Ada gave Nessa the difficult outside exchange and accepted her suggested mark.

memoryRef.anchor: Ada remembered that same old wait on the outdoor track; she was standing indoors now.

hooks: Imani aligned the crescent notch with the old timing stencil, narrowing its purpose without identifying its maker.
An archived form showed the same four boxes beside the words NEXT SERIES, but the series itself was unnamed.
The unexplained blue cord still hung from the clock handle while they practised.
chapters.plan: After the trial, Nessa planned to call the absent captain, but her phone remained in her bag.
chapters.hypothesis: If the last exchange were late, their trial would fail; the next exchange had not happened yet.
chapters.dream: Ada recalled last night’s dream of floating lanes and recognised it as a dream, not a memory of this track.
chapters.uncertainty: A distant spectator might have been the former captain, but the runners could not recognise the face.

chapters.title: The Clock After the Finish

facts.subject: char:ada
facts.anchor: Ada remained in the officials’ room after the results were posted.

facts.subject: item:relay_card
facts.anchor: Imani returned the intact relay card to Ada in the officials’ room.

facts.subject: org:relay_team
facts.anchor: The fifteen-pound return fare took their travel fund from ninety pounds down to seventy-five.

facts.subject: char:nessa
facts.anchor: The runners elected Nessa team captain after the race.

facts.subject: char:ada
facts.object: closed pink line on left palm
facts.anchor: The scrape on Ada’s left palm was closed now, a pink line that no longer needed a dressing.

facts.subject: item:timing_clock
facts.anchor: The timing clock rested on the desk in the officials’ room.

facts.subject: item:brass_key
facts.anchor: Ada returned the single brass key to Imani before leaving the cabinet.

facts.subject: item:relay_card
facts.anchor: The signed result placed their relay team second, with no appeal pending.

claim: “Second is enough for me,” Nessa said, speaking only for herself.
trueClaim: Seventy-five pounds will get us home.
“Seventy-five pounds will get us home,” Ada said, reading the fare beside the counted notes.

cognitions.content: The notch belongs to the timing stencil, not to a secret disqualification code.
cognitions.anchor: Ada read the stencil instructions and learned that the notch positioned the timing grid.

cognitions.content: The team can return for another meet.
cognitions.anchor: Nessa believed they could return for another meet, although no entry had been paid.

cognitions.content: The cord came from an earlier travelling team.
cognitions.anchor: Imani suspected a travelling team had left the cord, but had no name or date.

cognitions.content: The notch meant their entry had already been rejected.
cognitions.anchor: Ada admitted her earlier false belief that the notch marked an already rejected entry.

correction.content: The notch positions a timing grid and does not reject the entry.
correction.anchor: The printed instructions corrected that fear: the notch positioned the grid and carried no verdict.

relationship: Ada asked Nessa to plan the next season with her rather than simply fill a vacant lane.
memory: Before she joined this adult club, Nessa had been a school sprinter.
hooks: The stencil instructions finally explained the crescent notch: it positioned the timing grid.
The four NEXT SERIES boxes were still empty when Ada filed the card; nobody knew which series they meant.
Inside the knot Imani found a tiny sewn number, 41, but no team name and no explanation.
chapters.plan: Nessa intended to enter the next series next month; she made no entry that evening.
chapters.hypothesis: If another team withdrew, second place might become first, but no team had withdrawn.
chapters.dream: For a moment Ada imagined Roland applauding from the doorway; she knew the doorway was empty.
chapters.uncertainty: Number 41 could have identified a team or an inventory batch; neither explanation was confirmed.
